attributes.residual:
BEST RETAINED: UNCHANGED at real 126, T204/O204, multiset 0t, 61 differing words. No source change kept.

WHAT THIS ADDS TO MC's CAP, which screened the postprocessor side only. The residual is now named at source level and it is ONE FACT: a parameters-versus-locals BLOCK ROTATION in the callee-saved numbering, with the locals already in correct relative order and the interference graph provably identical between the two builds (the opcode streams are identical at 204/204, so the live ranges are isomorphic and the only possible input difference is the allocator's node ORDERING). That is why MC's +0xcc web refuses to bind: quad is r25 in the target and r28 in ours purely because the whole local block sits three registers higher in our colouring.

WHY THE SOURCE AXIS IS CAPPED AND NOT MERELY UNFINISHED. Three distinct axes, three different failure modes, all measured: declaration order among initialised locals reaches codegen but only schedules the stores (D1); initialiser position folds away before codegen and is categorically unreachable (D2); declaration order does perturb the colouring but only locally and in the wrong direction (D3). None of the three can express 'move the parameter block above the local block', because parameter numbering is not a function of any declaration the source can reorder - the ABI fixes their order and C offers no way to declare them relative to locals. The scope note on claim.law.SP_initializer-presence-outranks-declaration-position-in-callee-saved-numbering.20260901.v1 should be read as BOUNDED by this: its two-pass rule was measured on show_piles, a function whose parameters were not in the callee-saved contest, and it does not extend to a function where they are.

hypothesis.cheapest_refuting_observation: Buildless and free: `python tools/gdl/fnasm.py game/sys/memcard drawMemCardMessage --ours` and locate every USE of our r30 (savedBusy) and the target's r27, then compare the two live ranges end to end. If savedBusy's first definition and last use sit at the same instruction indices in both streams - which the identical 204/204 opcode streams make likely - then the live ranges are already identical, no source change can shorten one without changing the instruction stream, and the priority theory is refuted outright: the rotation is then a pure allocator tie-break with no source lever, and the function should be recorded as source-exhausted and handed to the class-widening decision that MC's cap already escalated to the user.
hypothesis.screened_against_target: partly - the correspondence table above IS screened against target bytes and is the solid part. What is NOT screened is the live-range claim: no per-register use census was taken for r30/r27 this run, and that census is buildless, which is exactly why it is nominated as the cheapest refuting observation rather than left as a probe.
hypothesis.statement: The rotation is decided by allocation PRIORITY, not by declaration order, and priority here is plausibly a function of live-range length or use count rather than symbol-table position - which is why no reordering of declarations moves it. The one source-level lever that has NOT been tried, and the only one that could change priority without changing semantics, is altering the NUMBER of simultaneously-live callee-saved values so the allocator's packing changes: our colouring leaves r27 and r31 unused while the target leaves r23 and r24 unused, and both use exactly ten registers, so the two builds are packing the same ten values into different holes. Concretely: check whether `savedBusy` genuinely needs a callee-saved home across the whole function, or whether the target's source read gGameBusy later (nearer its single use), which would shorten that live range and free the top of the range for the parameter block.
